newsitem.title: UK: Swiss trade sees Brazil 97/98 coffee at 28 mln.
newsitem.headline: Swiss trade sees Brazil 97/98 coffee at 28 mln.

text.p: Brazil's coffee harvest could reach 27.5 to 28 million 60-kg bags in 1997/98, down from a revised 30-31 million in 1996/97, Swiss traders said.
The traders, speaking to Reuters, put the 1998/99 crop even higher but in a wide 35-45 million range.
In the previous survey in December, the Swiss traders put the 1997/98 crop at above 30 million and 1996/97's at 27 million.
In 1995/96, Brazil had a weather-hit crop of 12.5 million bags.
In the latest estimate, one trader put world's 1997/98 consumption at around 97 million bags, thus resulting in a surplus of four to five million bags for the year.
The new Swiss forecast for 1997/98 was in line with the U.S. Department of Agriculture's estimate, released on June 13, which put the Brazilian crop of 28 million.
"The USDA could be very near to the truth," said a trader at a large Swiss trade house.

But the fact that the USDA left the 1996/97 estimate of 27.50 million unchanged came as a surprise to many crop watchers in Switzerland, home to one of the world's largest coffee traders and roasters.
Brazilian officials and traders had earlier voiced a reservation over the USDA's forecast of 28 million bags, saying that the estimate lacked a credible methodology and ran counter to crop cycles.
The Brazilian government has said it is working with a 1997/98 crop estimate of 22 million bags against 25 to 26 million bags in 1996/97.

The USDA has defended its forecast, saying the high number reflected a number of factors including generally good growing conditions, an increased number of bearing trees and sharply higher prices than a year ago. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
